title: Reliability-aware BERT-based Emotion Classification via Probability Calibration and Selective Prediction
abstract: Deep neural language models often produce over-confident predictions, limiting their reliability in real-world decision-making, particularly under class imbalance. In this work, we investigate probability calibration and uncertainty-aware selective prediction for emotion classification using a Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT)-based model. Experiments are conducted on the Emotions dataset, which exhibits natural class imbalance across six emotion categories. We adopt a multi-stage pipeline comprising dataset preparation, baseline fine-tuning, post-hoc probability calibration via temperature scaling, uncertainty estimation using probability-based metrics, and selective prediction based on uncertainty thresholds. Results show that temperature scaling further improves probability calibration, reducing expected calibration error from 0.0051 to 0.0035 (a relative reduction of approximately 31%) and tightening reliability diagrams, without degrading classification accuracy. Uncertainty measures such as predictive entropy and probability margin effectively distinguish correct from incorrect predictions, with misclassified samples exhibiting higher uncertainty. Leveraging these uncertainty estimates, selective prediction achieves a favorable risk-coverage trade-off: predictive risk decreases while accuracy on the accepted subset increases as coverage is reduced. At an operating point of approximately 90% coverage, the model attains substantially improved reliability with minimal loss in coverage. These findings demonstrate that calibrated uncertainty estimates enable robust selective prediction and provide a principled framework for deploying emotion classification systems in reliability-critical applications.
